officialTitle: Dutch-Belgian Randomized Lung Cancer Screening Trial (NELSON): volume CT screening versus no screening

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: A total of 13,195 men (primary analysis) and 2594 women (subgroup analyses) between the ages of 50 and 74 were randomly assigned to undergo CT screening at T0 (baseline), year 1, year 3, and year 5.5 or no screening.
design.notes: Sample size reflects the male primary-analysis population; women were analysed as a subgroup. Volume-based nodule management.

sponsor: Netherlands Organization of Health Research and Development and others
clinicalQuestion: Does volume-based low-dose CT screening reduce lung-cancer mortality compared with no screening in high-risk current and former smokers?

pico.population: High-risk current and former smokers in the Netherlands and Belgium (men as primary population; women as subgroup)
pico.intervention: Volume CT screening at baseline and at increasing intervals
pico.outcomes: Lung-cancer mortality at 10 years; lung cancer incidence; referral rates

arms.label: Volume CT screening
arms.regimen: Low-dose volume CT screening at baseline and subsequent rounds

publications.title: Reduced Lung-Cancer Mortality with Volume CT Screening in a Randomized Trial.
publications.label: Primary analysis (10-year follow-up)

outcomes.endpointLabel: Cumulative lung-cancer mortality rate ratio at 10 years
outcomes.sourceQuote: The cumulative rate ratio for death from lung cancer at 10 years was 0.76 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.61 to 0.94; P = 0.01) in the screening group as compared with the control group, similar to the values at years 8 and 9.
lung-cancer mortality was 2.50 deaths per 1000 person-years and 3.30 deaths per 1000 person-years, respectively.

outcomes.endpointLabel: Lung-cancer mortality rate ratio at 10 years
outcomes.sourceQuote: Among women, the rate ratio was 0.67 (95% CI, 0.38 to 1.14) at 10 years of follow-up, with values of 0.41 to 0.52 in years 7 through 9.

strengths: Minimum follow-up of a decade via national registry linkage
Volume-based nodule management with low referral rate
limitations: Primary analysis restricted to men; women analysed as an underpowered subgroup
Screening intervals differed from annual schedules used elsewhere

clinicalImplications.text: Confirmed in a European population that CT screening of high-risk smokers reduces lung-cancer mortality versus no screening, and supported volume-based nodule management as a way to limit follow-up procedures.

tumourBoardPearl.text: NELSON compared CT with no screening (NLST used chest radiography as control) and popularised volumetric nodule assessment to curb false-positive work-ups.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 31995683. Registry identifier is the Netherlands Trial Register number printed in the abstract.
